paragraphs: The R63 AMG was produced for an extremely limited run from 2006 to 2007 as the flagship of the R-Class range. It uses the M156 - a 6.2-litre naturally aspirated V8 that was AMG's first entirely in-house developed engine. The M156 is shared with several other AMG models of the era, including the C63, E63, and ML63, and is known for its distinctive naturally aspirated character. The R63 AMG is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every R63 AMG on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the R63 AMG from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the R63 AMG was produced in extremely limited numbers with the M156 V8, engine matching is critical for a successful rebuild or replacement. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic R-Class quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
